title: Homeostasis and Feedback in Body Systems Review Test
description: Review practice for homeostasis and feedback in body systems.

questions.prompt: A runner's heart rate rises during exercise and lowers during rest. What does this pattern show?
questions.questionText: A runner's heart rate rises during exercise and lowers during rest. What does this pattern show?
options: Body systems can adjust to changing cell needs.
The circulatory system disappears during rest.
Cells stop needing materials during exercise.
Heart rate is unrelated to activity.
questions.correctAnswer: Body systems can adjust to changing cell needs.
questions.explanation: Heart rate changes help deliver materials when cells need more energy.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best shows a feedback pathway for body temperature?
questions.questionText: Which sequence best shows a feedback pathway for body temperature?
options: stimulus -> receptors -> signals -> control center -> response
control center -> no signals -> no body change
questions.correctAnswer: stimulus -> receptors -> signals -> control center -> response
questions.explanation: Feedback uses detection, signaling, processing, and response.

questions.prompt: A person sweats on a hot day. Which function does sweating support?
questions.questionText: A person sweats on a hot day. Which function does sweating support?
questions.explanation: Sweating helps remove heat as water evaporates from skin.

questions.prompt: Which body systems interact when breathing rate increases during exercise?
questions.questionText: Which body systems interact when breathing rate increases during exercise?
options: respiratory, circulatory, muscular, and nervous systems
questions.correctAnswer: respiratory, circulatory, muscular, and nervous systems
questions.explanation: Exercise responses involve several interacting systems.

questions.prompt: A student says, "The body responds randomly to changes." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
questions.questionText: A student says, "The body responds randomly to changes." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
options: Heart rate and breathing rate predictably rise during activity.
questions.correctAnswer: Heart rate and breathing rate predictably rise during activity.

questions.prompt: A model shows low water level in the body -> thirst -> drinking water. What does the model show?
questions.questionText: A model shows low water level in the body -> thirst -> drinking water. What does the model show?
options: a response that helps restore internal balance
questions.correctAnswer: a response that helps restore internal balance
questions.explanation: Thirst can help the body respond to low water levels.

questions.prompt: Which evidence supports that the nervous system helps regulate responses?
questions.questionText: Which evidence supports that the nervous system helps regulate responses?
options: The nervous system is always visible from outside.
Bones create nerve signals without cells.
Signals from receptors are processed before muscles or glands respond.
questions.correctAnswer: Signals from receptors are processed before muscles or glands respond.
questions.explanation: Receptors and signals help the body detect and respond to changes.

questions.prompt: A person shivers in cold air. Which explanation best connects systems and cells?
questions.questionText: A person shivers in cold air. Which explanation best connects systems and cells?
options: Muscle activity produces heat that helps maintain conditions for cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Muscle activity produces heat that helps maintain conditions for cells.
questions.explanation: Shivering uses muscles to produce heat.

questions.prompt: Which data would best show that the body responds to exercise?
questions.questionText: Which data would best show that the body responds to exercise?
options: pulse and breathing rate before, during, and after exercise
number of windows in the gym
questions.correctAnswer: pulse and breathing rate before, during, and after exercise
questions.explanation: Pulse and breathing rate track body responses to changing activity.

questions.prompt: A student writes: stimulus -> response -> receptor -> brain. What correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student writes: stimulus -> response -> receptor -> brain. What correction is best?
options: The response should happen before detection.
Receptors detect the stimulus before the response.
The brain is always first before any stimulus exists.
questions.correctAnswer: Receptors detect the stimulus before the response.
questions.explanation: Detection comes before processing and response.

questions.prompt: Why is feedback important for multicellular organisms?
questions.questionText: Why is feedback important for multicellular organisms?
options: It prevents cells from needing materials.
It makes every system work alone.
It helps keep internal conditions within workable ranges for cells.
It stops all responses to the environment.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps keep internal conditions within workable ranges for cells.
questions.explanation: Cells need stable internal conditions to function.

questions.prompt: A person smells smoke and leaves a room. Which part of the pathway is the stimulus?
questions.questionText: A person smells smoke and leaves a room. Which part of the pathway is the stimulus?
questions.explanation: The stimulus is the environmental information detected by receptors.

questions.prompt: Which claim is supported when body temperature stays near 37 C in a warm and cool room?
questions.questionText: Which claim is supported when body temperature stays near 37 C in a warm and cool room?
options: The body can regulate internal temperature across different external conditions.
The room has no effect on the body.
Cells do not need stable conditions.
questions.correctAnswer: The body can regulate internal temperature across different external conditions.
questions.explanation: Maintaining similar internal temperature suggests regulation.

questions.prompt: A model leaves out blood flow during temperature regulation. What weakness does it have?
questions.questionText: A model leaves out blood flow during temperature regulation. What weakness does it have?
options: It misses one way heat can be moved around the body.
It proves blood is not involved in systems.
questions.correctAnswer: It misses one way heat can be moved around the body.
questions.explanation: Blood flow helps move heat and materials.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows a body response matching a stimulus?
questions.questionText: Which example best shows a body response matching a stimulus?
questions.explanation: Pupil size can respond to light level.
